taskRef.title: REC-14 (2026-10-29, read-only review, nothing changed) Legal search alignment. SeaweedFS has no `legal_documents` bucket (buckets: atlas-archive, atlas-artifacts, atlas-lake-dev, atlas-web-sources, langfuse, legal-evidence, poi-photos); `legal_documents` is a 3-row Postgres table and a 5-point Qdrant collection. The real legal corpus is Postgres `legal_chunks` (60,432 rows, 60,431 with 768-d embeddings, HNSW `legal_chunks_embedding_hnsw`, `tsv`, 0 summaries, 0 `qdrant_point_id`) joined to `legal_nodes` (35,106; 35,102 sections; citation_label/heading/node_path). MISALIGNED: `legal.find_similar_opinions` (`src/mcp/tools/legal-skills.tool.ts` ~L595) embeds via `/api/embed` and queries Qdrant `legal_documents`, so it searches 5 points and misses the 60k-chunk corpus; `legal.similar_cases` (~L293) is plainto_tsquery (AND of all words) over `cases` title+description with an inline to_tsvector (no index). Proposed alignment (proposal only): (1) find_similar_opinions -> Postgres `legal_chunks` HNSW cosine top-k + join `legal_nodes` (citation_label, heading), Qdrant optional; (2) verify the `legal_chunks` embedding recipe against `/api/embed` before mixing (no recipe census exists for legal_chunks); (3) similar_cases -> websearch_to_tsquery/OR semantics + a stored tsvector/GIN; (4) derived per-node/per-document embedding table `canonical=false`; (5) keep EmbeddingGemma 2 vectors in a separate index identity. `@atlas/duckdb` has no httpfs/S3 extension, so Parquet to SeaweedFS `atlas-lake-dev/v1` needs a proven-gap decision first.

recommendedDocChunks.title: GitHub - pgvector/pgvector: Open-source vector similarity search for Postgres · GitHub
headingPath: How many vectors can be stored in a single table?
Can I store vectors with different dimensions in the same column?
recommendedDocChunks.excerpt:
You can use
`vector`
as the type (instead of
`vector(n)`
).
```sql
CREATE TABLE embeddings (model_id bigint, item_id bigint, embedding vector, PRIMARY KEY (model_id, item_id));
```
However, you can only create indexes on rows with the same number of dimensions (using
expression
and
partial
indexing):
```sql
CREATE INDEX ON embeddings USING hnsw ((embedding::vector(3)) vector_l2_ops) WHERE (model_id = 123);
```
and query with:
```sql
SELECT * FROM embeddings WHERE model_id = 123 ORDER BY embedding::vector(3) <-> '[3,1,2]' LIMIT 5;
```
